events.title: Pilgrims Land at Plymouth
events.description: After weeks of exploring Cape Cod's coast, the Mayflower Pilgrims came ashore at what is now Plymouth, Massachusetts. There they founded Plymouth Colony.
events.significance: Plymouth became one of the earliest lasting English settlements in New England and a central story in American national memory.

events.title: A Doll's House Premieres in Copenhagen
events.description: Henrik Ibsen's play about a wife who walks out on her stifling marriage opened at the Royal Theatre in Copenhagen.
events.significance: Its challenge to Victorian ideas about marriage and women's roles caused a sensation. It is often called one of the most influential plays in modern theatre.

events.title: The Curies Discover Radium
events.description: Marie and Pierre Curie identified radium, a new radioactive element, in their research on uranium ore.
events.significance: The discovery opened the way to new cancer treatments and advances in atomic physics. It helped earn Marie Curie her place among history's great scientists.

events.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs Premieres
events.description: Walt Disney's film premiered at the Carthay Circle Theatre in Los Angeles. It was the first full-length cel-animated feature in film history.
events.significance: The film proved that animation could carry a feature-length story and launched the golden age of animated cinema.

events.title: Pan Am Flight 103 Bombed Over Lockerbie
events.description: A bomb exploded aboard Pan Am Flight 103 as it flew from Frankfurt toward Detroit via London. The plane fell on the Scottish town of Lockerbie.
events.significance: It was among the deadliest terrorist attacks involving aviation, and it led to major changes in international aviation security and counterterrorism cooperation.
